title: A Multi-Valued Homotopy-Theoretic Version of String Topology
content: String topology studies algebraic operations on the homology of free loop spaces and related mapping spaces. Its classical loop product is defined using an intersection condition at a marked point, an umkehr map associated with the diagonal of the underlying manifold, and concatenation of loops [1,2]. This paper develops a framework for a multi-valued homotopy-theoretic version of string topology. Instead of assigning a unique output loop to a pair of compatible loops, we allow a controlled family of admissible outputs. We represent such assignments by topological correspondences and use their graph projections to define induced homology maps whenever the required homological hypotheses hold. We formulate a candidate multi-valued loop product, prove its degree formula, establish homotopy invariance under admissible graph homotopies, and give a sufficient criterion for associativity. Examples illustrate the single-valued case, contractible families of choices, finite acyclic-valued models, and a failure of admissibility. We also discuss spectrum-level refinements, equivariant structures, and open problems. The framework is conditional: arbitrary multivalued maps do not automatically induce homology operations. The additional geometric, homological, and coherence hypotheses are made explicit throughout.
